tasks.name: Verify tread protection in place
tasks.notes: FIRST task. If tread protection is already in place from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC, verify integrity and repair any damaged sections. If no prior protection, install Ram Board Stair Armor. NEVER use plastic sheeting — extreme fall hazard per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2.

tasks.name: Install landing floor protection
tasks.notes: Canvas drop cloth runners at landing areas. Not needed on subfloor.

tasks.name: Mask walls for spray containment
tasks.notes: Tape & Drape pre-taped plastic along walls adjacent to railing. HVLP preferred over airless for in-place baluster work — significantly less overspray. Per doctrine 6.3.

tasks.name: Set up baluster spray containment
tasks.notes: Cardboard shields behind balusters, small torn tape pieces at baluster-rail junctions. Containment time depends on stairwell configuration and baluster count. Per doctrine 6.3.

sop_modules.name: Surface Preparation
sop_modules.notes: Prep varies by railing_type and substrate_state. Iron baluster solvent cleaning is FIRST prep step. Caulk after fill/sand, before primer. Bracket removal at QT4+.

tasks.name: Solvent clean iron balusters (SSPC-SP 1)
tasks.notes: MANDATORY first prep step for ALL iron/steel balusters regardless of substrate_state. Removes manufacturing oils and drawing compounds. Failure causes fish-eye defects and delamination. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.4 and SSPC-SP 1.

tasks.name: Scuff-sand powder-coated iron balusters
tasks.notes: Scuff-sand with 180-220 grit (Scotch-Brite pads recommended for conformable profile coverage). Creates mechanical tooth for bonding primer adhesion. Per doctrine 4.4.

tasks.name: Sand wood balusters per substrate
tasks.notes: Bare substrates: 150-220 grit depending on substrate. Factory-primed: scuff sand 150-180 grit. Balusters are first wood component prepped per canonical sequence (#5). Profile complexity affects time (square < turned).

tasks.name: Sand newel posts per substrate
tasks.notes: Bare substrates: 150-220 grit. Factory-primed: scuff sand. Newels are larger with more detail (caps, rosettes, flutes). Newels prepped after balusters per canonical sequence (#6).

tasks.name: Sand handrails per substrate
tasks.notes: Bare substrates: 150-220 grit on all 4 surfaces (top, 2 sides, underside). Factory-primed: scuff sand. Handrails last per canonical sequence (#7).

tasks.name: Sand base rails per substrate
tasks.notes: Conditional — not all railing systems have base rails. Same sanding protocol as handrails.

tasks.name: Remove sanding dust (tack cloth / vacuum)
tasks.notes: Thorough dust removal after all sanding. Tack cloth all surfaces. Vacuum treads/landings.

tasks.name: Fill fastener holes and sand smooth
tasks.notes: Fill nail/screw holes on wood components (balusters, newels primarily). QT3: fill obvious holes. QT4: fill all visible. QT5: fill all regardless of size. Sand flush with 220 grit.

tasks.name: Caulk newel junction joints
tasks.notes: Caulk at newel-to-tread junction and newel-to-handrail junction. Fills visible gaps. Paintable acrylic latex caulk. Per EA newel (typically 2-3 joints per newel).

tasks.name: Remove handrail brackets (label and bag)
tasks.notes: QT4+ only. Remove handrail brackets, label each piece, bag hardware. Mark locations. Allows handrail to be finished horizontally (reduces runs/sags) and paint behind attachment points. At QT3 brackets are masked in place. Per doctrine 12.1.

sop_modules.name: Primer Application
sop_modules.notes: CONDITIONAL — only runs when substrate_state = SS_BARE or SS_POWDER_COATED. Factory-primed substrates skip this module. Primer type driven by substrate and railing_type. Canonical sequence within: balusters → newels → handrails → base rails.

tasks.name: Prime balusters
tasks.notes: Primer type depends on railing_type: all_wood → SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_STANDARD (or substrate-specific variant). iron_and_wood + SS_BARE → SYS_PRIMER_IRON_DTM. iron_and_wood + SS_POWDER_COATED → SYS_PRIMER_POWDER_COAT_BOND. Balusters first per canonical sequence (#5).

tasks.name: Prime newel posts
tasks.notes: Wood primer per substrate. Newels after balusters per canonical sequence (#6). All newels are wood regardless of railing_type.

tasks.name: Prime handrails
tasks.notes: Wood primer per substrate. All 4 surfaces (top, 2 sides, underside). Handrails after newels per canonical sequence (#7). QT4+: handrails may be horizontal (bracket removal) for easier priming.

tasks.name: Prime base rails
tasks.notes: Conditional. Same primer system as handrails. After handrails in sequence.

tasks.name: Light sand primer for adhesion
tasks.notes: 220 grit light sand entire primed surface for finish coat adhesion. Tack cloth after sanding.

sop_modules.name: Finish Coat Application
sop_modules.notes: Finish coat in canonical sequence: balusters (#5), newels (#6), handrails (#7), base rails. Brush is default. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). For turned balusters: use German round trim brushes + flow additive.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on balusters
tasks.notes: Balusters first per canonical sequence (#5). In two-tone systems: light color on balusters first. Square: angled sash brush. Turned: German round trim brush with flow additive to prevent roping. Thin coats essential — profile traps paint.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on newel posts
tasks.notes: Newels after balusters per canonical sequence (#6). Larger surface area — 2-2.5 inch angled sash. Detail work on caps, rosettes, flutes. Thin coats on vertical surfaces.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on handrails
tasks.notes: Handrails last per canonical sequence (#7). In two-tone systems: darker rail color applied last covers overlap at baluster-rail junction. QT4+: paint horizontally (brackets removed). All 4 surfaces: top, 2 sides, underside.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on base rails
tasks.notes: Conditional — when system has base rail. After handrails. 3 accessible surfaces.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on balusters
tasks.notes: Balusters first per canonical sequence. HVLP preferred. Cardboard shields behind each baluster. 6-8 inch distance, light passes. Bottom-to-top for primer coats. Containment masking must be in place.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on newel posts
tasks.notes: Newels after balusters. Larger target — easier spray than balusters but more material.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on handrails
tasks.notes: Handrails last per canonical sequence. Light passes on all 4 surfaces. Watch for runs on underside.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on base rails
tasks.notes: Conditional — when system has base rail. After handrails.

sop_modules.name: Between-Coat Interstage
sop_modules.notes: Runs after every coat EXCEPT the final coat. Universal at ALL quality tiers. Sanding discipline varies by QT: QT3=spot only, QT4=full 220, QT5=full 220-320. Baluster junction nib removal critical.

tasks.name: Clean work area between coats
tasks.notes: Remove dust, debris from treads and landings. Ensure clean environment for next coat.

tasks.name: Inspect previous coat
tasks.notes: QT3: quick scan at 6ft — obvious defects on balusters/newels/handrails. QT4: systematic scan at 3ft — all visible defects marked. QT5: critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance. Pay special attention to baluster-handrail junctions and handrail underside.

tasks.name: Sand between coats
tasks.notes: QT3: spot sand nibs/rough spots only. QT4: full 220 grit all surfaces. QT5: thorough 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern. Junction nibs at baluster-handrail connection must be removed at QT4+. Rigid sanding block on flat handrail surfaces (FFD 15.4.1).

tasks.name: Patch and repair marked defects
tasks.notes: Fill, sand, and spot-prime any defects found during inspection. Scope varies by QT.

tasks.name: Spot coat patched areas
tasks.notes: Touch-up patched areas to match surrounding finish before next full coat.

tasks.name: Tack cloth all surfaces
tasks.notes: Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth before next coat application.

tasks.name: Final quality inspection
tasks.notes: QT3: scan for obvious defects. QT4: systematic review of all components. QT5: critical inspection at arm's length. Check: baluster-handrail junctions, newel detail, handrail all 4 surfaces, caulk lines, finish uniformity.

tasks.name: Feel test on handrails
tasks.notes: QT5 only. Run hand along entire handrail length. Must feel glass-smooth — no nibs, no rough spots, no drip ridges. Handrails are the most-touched surface in any home. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine.

tasks.name: Touch-up defects found during final inspection
tasks.notes: Correct any remaining defects. Feather touch-ups into surrounding finish.

tasks.name: Apply polyurethane topcoat on handrails
tasks.notes: Optional QT5 upgrade. Water-based polyurethane clear coat over cured enamel finish on handrails ONLY. Provides maximum hand-oil resistance. Allow full enamel cure (typically 24-48 hours) before poly application. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.1.

tasks.name: Reinstall handrail brackets
tasks.notes: QT4+ only. Reinstall labeled brackets in original locations. Touch-up attachment point paint after reinstall.

tasks.name: Remove spray containment
tasks.notes: Remove cardboard shields, Tape & Drape. Spray method only.

tasks.name: Remove wall masking
tasks.notes: Score tape edge before removal. Pull at 45-degree angle.

tasks.name: Remove floor protection at landings
tasks.notes: Remove canvas drops from landing areas.

tasks.name: Remove tread protection
tasks.notes: LAST task. Remove Ram Board Stair Armor carefully. Score tape edges. May DEFER removal if tread work (SF_STAIR_TREAD_NC) follows — tread protection continuity is critical.

tasks.name: Clean tools and equipment
tasks.notes: Clean brushes (including German round brushes), spray equipment, dispose of consumables. Water cleanup for waterborne products.

zones.notes: Mandatory from Day 1. Verify if already in place from riser spec. Removal may be deferred.

workflow_sequence.standard_bare: MOD_STRL_SETUP → MOD_STRL_PREP → MOD_STRL_PRIME → MOD_STRL_INTERSTAGE → MOD_STRL_FINISH_COAT(1) → MOD_STRL_INTERSTAGE → MOD_STRL_FINISH_COAT(2) → MOD_STRL_FINAL_INSPECT → MOD_STRL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.standard_factory_primed: MOD_STRL_SETUP → MOD_STRL_PREP → MOD_STRL_FINISH_COAT(1) → MOD_STRL_INTERSTAGE → MOD_STRL_FINISH_COAT(2) → MOD_STRL_FINAL_INSPECT → MOD_STRL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.standard_powder_coated: MOD_STRL_SETUP → MOD_STRL_PREP → MOD_STRL_PRIME → MOD_STRL_INTERSTAGE → MOD_STRL_FINISH_COAT(1) → MOD_STRL_INTERSTAGE → MOD_STRL_FINISH_COAT(2) → MOD_STRL_FINAL_INSPECT → MOD_STRL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.qt5_brush_roll: MOD_STRL_SETUP → MOD_STRL_PREP → [MOD_STRL_PRIME] → [MOD_STRL_INTERSTAGE] → MOD_STRL_FINISH_COAT(1) → MOD_STRL_INTERSTAGE → MOD_STRL_FINISH_COAT(2) → MOD_STRL_INTERSTAGE → MOD_STRL_FINISH_COAT(3) → MOD_STRL_FINAL_INSPECT → MOD_STRL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.notes: Prime module conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE or SS_POWDER_COATED. QT5 brush/roll adds additional FINISH_COAT + INTERSTAGE cycle. Within each coat module: balusters before newels before handrails before base rails per canonical sequence.

canonical_sequence_enforcement.rule: Balusters (#5) MUST be completed before newels (#6), newels before handrails (#7) within every module
canonical_sequence_enforcement.rationale: In two-tone systems, the darker rail paint applied last covers overlap at the baluster-rail junction — saves enormous cutting-in time. In same-color systems, the sequence minimizes wet-edge contact risk.
